Command: Rest on the first day of Unleavened Bread
Summary: The first day of Unleavened Bread is a holy convocation of rest, opening the seven days of unleavened bread.
Commandment: Keep the first day of Unleavened Bread as a holy convocation and rest on it.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The opening rest tied the feast week to the haste of the departure from Egypt. Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: To rehearse God's saving acts at appointed seasons (Leviticus 23); Paul calls Christ our Passover (1 Corinthians 5:7).
Function: The feast week opened with a day of rest, a holy convocation — and that set-apart day is what makes this ceremonial. Its goal was to open the seven days of unleavened bread in worship rather than work, tying the feast to the haste of the departure from Egypt. It addressed no particular evil — its work was remembrance, not restraint. The rest said the week belonged to God first, and the bread and the memory followed from that.
